source.title: Abnormalities in the awareness and control of action
source.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B

confidence_rationale: The fuller review behind the 2002 TICS framework, with the added value of a localisation claim: representations of the CURRENT and PREDICTED state of the motor system are in parietal cortex, while representations of INTENDED movements are in prefrontal/premotor cortex. This dissociates the predicted-state machinery (SD-030 comparator substrate) from the intention/goal machinery (E3-side), which is exactly the separation REE draws between the self-forward-model and the goal/viability evaluator. Held at 0.68 because the lesion synthesis is correlational and the parietal/prefrontal localisation is coarse relative to REE's z_self/z_goal split.
failure_signatures: Phantom-limb and anosognosic movement illusions are driven by motor-command streams in the ABSENCE of sensory confirmation -- a self-model that represents agency from intention alone, with no observed-self to compare against, will hallucinate successful action, the failure SD-030's residual is meant to catch.

Damage dissociates 'predicted current state' (parietal) from 'intended movement' (prefrontal/premotor); collapsing these into one representation -- as V3 does by running E2 on combined z_gamma with no z_self stream -- removes the distinction agency depends on.

Delusions of control arise when intention and the felt consequence of action are no longer properly linked: the comparator between intended and achieved self-state has failed, the MECH-215 (2) E2-self-transition prerequisite breaking.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Awareness of action is based on two sources -- sensory signals from skin/muscle and the stream of issued motor commands. Representations of the current and predicted state of the motor system reside in parietal cortex; representations of intended actions in prefrontal/premotor cortex. Lesions dissociate these, producing phantom limbs, anosognosia, utilization behaviour, and delusions of control.
mapping.ree_translation: The parietal current/predicted-state representation is the substrate of SD-030's z_self forward model (the predicted self-state E2_self emits); the prefrontal/premotor intended-action representation maps to REE's goal/intention side (z_goal -> E3). The paper's central dissociation -- predicted-state machinery separable from intention machinery -- is the biological warrant for keeping the SD-030 self-forward-model distinct from the E3 viability/goal evaluator, and for MECH-215's claim that an E2 self-transition model must exist as the subject of agentive prediction.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Lesion-and-illusion synthesis, not a mechanistic recording; the parietal/prefrontal localisation is at a far coarser grain than REE's z_self vs z_goal latent split, so the mapping is a functional-architecture analogy. The clinical phenomena are predictions REE should reproduce, not evidence about REE's current substrate. SD-030 remains V4-deferred; literature_confidence only.
mapping.source_context: Human cognitive neurology review; integrates lesion data (phantom limb, anosognosia, delusions of control) into a forward-model account.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (Phil Trans R Soc B review, PMC1692910; the deeper companion to the 2002 TICS piece). Mapping fidelity good -- the predicted-state-vs-intention dissociation is genuinely informative for REE's self-model/goal separation -- but coarser-grained than the latent architecture, hence below the 2002 entry. Transfer risk low-moderate.
